outcome: No exact value of any Van der Waerden number was newly determined between 26 January 2024 and 13 October 2026 as far as I could find; the movement is in bounds and in one related difference result: a two-colour lower bound (1-o(1))k·2^(k-1) for all k (Campos, Fox and Schildkraut, arXiv 2608.20824, 21 Aug 2026, whose coloring and proof the authors credit to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro), a three-colour super-exponential lower bound (Fox and Hunter, arXiv 2606.02541, 1 Jun 2026), a Lean-checked proof by DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus that W(k+1)-W(k) tends to infinity (forum post 10 Apr 2026), off-diagonal and multicolour bounds (Cao, arXiv 2609.31798, 25 Sep 2026), and two repository claims from July 2026 (new lower bounds for W(3,19)-W(3,25), and a Lean re-verification of the 1978 value W(2,5)=178) that have not been reviewed by a mathematician.
problem_asks: Unpacked from the statement 'The values of the Van der Waerden numbers'. (1) For each number of colours r and progression length k, the exact value of W(r,k), the least N such that every r-colouring of {1,...,N} contains a monochromatic k-term arithmetic progression. The statement names no particular (r,k), so it asks for all of them, i.e. the complete table of values. (2) On the article's own scope, also the off-diagonal numbers w(r; k_1,...,k_r), where each colour carries its own progression length; each is a separate value the article tabulates, and the bullet's link target covers them. (3) The verb is 'values': determining exact values is what is asked. A bound on W(r,k) is not a value, so a bound moves this problem only if it fixes a value. The trivial cases W(1,k)=k and W(r,2)=r+1 are noted in the article and are not asked. Known exact values (the article lists seven nontrivial ones: W(2,3)=9, W(2,4)=35, W(2,5)=178, W(2,6)=1132, W(3,3)=27, W(3,4)=293, W(4,3)=76) do not answer item (1), which quantifies over all r and k.

events.what_happened: Berlekamp's 1968 construction gives a two-colour lower bound W(2,p+1) > p·2^p for prime p. Cited in the Wikipedia article and as the k-1 prime case in the Campos-Fox-Schildkraut abstract. I did not open the 1968 paper, and the venue and title are from background knowledge, not from a source I read; the statement itself is taken from the two sources cited.
events.delivers: Lower bound for the two-colour diagonal numbers W(2,k) at k = p+1 for primes p only. Two colours; diagonal; lower bound only.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: no exact value, no bound for other k, no other colour counts.
events.directly_checkable: A colouring of an interval of length p·2^p avoiding a monochromatic (p+1)-term progression is explicit; not checked by me.
events.direction: Cuts toward growth of the diagonal numbers: W(2,p+1) is at least p·2^p, a lower bound. No object contradicts anything the problem asserts.
events.object: Explicit 2-colouring family from Berlekamp's algebraic construction (as cited): an interval of length p·2^p with no monochromatic (p+1)-term progression, for each prime p.

events.what_happened: Gowers's proof of Szemeredi's theorem gives the best known upper bound on W(r,k) as cited in the article and on the Erdos problem 138 page: W(k) <= 2^(2^(2^(2^(2^(k+9))))) for two colours. Cited, not opened.
events.delivers: Upper bound (tower-type) on the two-colour numbers W(2,k) for every k. It moves no exact value.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: upper bound only, and very far from exact.
events.direction: Upper bound on the numbers; cuts against nothing asserted.

events.what_happened: Shelah (1988) proved that the van der Waerden numbers are primitive recursive, as the Wikipedia article states. Cited, not opened.
events.delivers: Qualitative growth bound (primitive recursive) on W(r,k) for all r and k. No value.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.direction: Growth bound only; cuts against nothing asserted.

events.what_happened: On the Erdos 138 forum thread, Adam Zsolt Wagner posted on 10 Apr 2026 that 'The DeepMind prover agent has found a Lean proof for the difference variant', with the claim W(k+1) >= W(k)+k and a link to a Lean file in a fork of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (mo271, commit 2f7fa0e). The Lean theorem erdos_138.variants.difference states answer(True) <-> Tendsto (fun k => W(k+1) - W k) atTop, proved by 'exact iff_of_true trivial W_diff_tendsto'; its docstring reads 'The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal proof of this statement.' The AlphaProof Nexus preprint (arXiv:2605.22763, 21 May 2026) lists problem 138 as an asterisked variant resolved by its full-featured agent in Table 1, and the Science publication is reported for 8 Oct 2026 by secondary sources only. This concerns the gaps W(k+1)-W(k), not the values; it answers the second of Erdos's two difference questions, not W(k)^(1/k) tending to infinity.
events.revisions: Forum post 10 Apr 2026; AlphaProof Nexus preprint arXiv:2605.22763v1 (21 May 2026) reports it in Table 1; Science publication reported 8 Oct 2026 (secondary only, not verified).
events.delivers: W(k+1)-W(k) tends to infinity for the two-colour numbers (the Lean statement), with the quantitative form W(k+1) >= W(k)+k as stated in the forum post; the inequality's helper lemma W_diff_tendsto was not read. Restricted to two colours and to the difference variant. Does not determine any value and does not give W(k)^(1/k) tending to infinity.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: no value of any W(r,k) is determined, and the growth question for W(k)^(1/k) is untouched.

events.what_happened: J. Fox and Z. Hunter, 'Three-color van der Waerden numbers grow super-exponentially', arXiv:2606.02541 (submitted 1 Jun 2026, single version, 19 pages). Abstract: for k sufficiently large there is a 3-colouring of about the first 2^(k log*k /4) integers with no monochromatic k-term progression, so w(k;3) > 2^(k log* k /4) (Theorem 1), and a new lower bound on multicolour van der Waerden numbers resolving an Erdos-Graham problem on canonical van der Waerden numbers. The erdosproblems.com entry for 138 cites it as FoHu26. Abstract and HTML read; the PDF body was unreadable through the fetch tool.
events.delivers: Three colours, large k: W(k,3) grows faster than any exponential in k (for the three-colour numbers only). The multicolour canonical result is stated in the abstract as resolving the Erdos-Graham question; its scope beyond the abstract was not read. The two-colour growth question of Erdos (the 500-dollar prize) is not addressed by this paper; the abstract does not mention two colours.

events.directly_checkable: The colouring is said to be explicit in the abstract's wording 'we show that there is a three-coloring' (existence). Whether the construction is explicit was not established by me.
events.direction: Lower bound cuts toward growth of three-colour numbers; no value; no conflict with the problem's assertion.
events.object: Three-colouring of an initial segment of length about 2^(k log* k / 4) with no monochromatic k-term progression, for k sufficiently large. Stated as an existence result in the abstract; explicitness not established.

The README says 'Work by Claude (Fable 5) with Abigail Haddad, July 2026' and 'Everything in this repo was produced by an AI (Claude)'; it names Haddad as a data scientist, not a mathematician, and states 'NOT CHECKED BY A MATHEMATICIAN; COULD BE WRONG'. The README also says a mathematician later called these 'easy-direction results'. Read through a summarising fetch; the code was not read.

The bounds rest on a computer scan and code not read by me.

events.what_happened: M. Campos, J. Fox and C. Schildkraut, 'A new lower bound for two-color van der Waerden numbers', arXiv:2608.20824 (submitted 21 Aug 2026, single version, math.CO and math.NT). Main result (Theorem 1): w(k) >= (1-o(1))·k·2^(k-1) for all positive integers k, verifying a conjecture of Erdos and extending Berlekamp's 1968 bound from k-1 prime to all k. The construction combines colourings c_p for various primes p (Lemma 4), with s = sum of the primes and Q = product of (2^p-1). The abstract and AI-use paragraph state that the coloring used to prove Theorem 1 and a proof of Theorem 1 were generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, and that 'the proof we present, while drawing somewhat on the proof given by ChatGPT, was produced by the authors'. The paper thanks Zach Hunter for comments. Read from the arXiv HTML via a summarising fetch; the PDF body was unreadable.
events.delivers: A lower bound of asymptotic form (1-o(1))·k·2^(k-1) for the two-colour diagonal numbers W(2,k), for every k in the asymptotic sense. Two colours only; lower bound only; no exact value for any k; the (1-o(1)) form means it does not decide any specific entry. By my arithmetic from the article table, k·2^(k-1) is below each displayed lower bound for k = 7 to 11 (for example 448 against '>3,703' at k=7), so no displayed table entry changes; the comparison is not meaningful at small k because of the (1-o(1)) factor.
events.remains: All exact values of W(2,k) for k >= 3 (including those not yet known: the article shows only W(2,3) to W(2,6) exact); the upper bounds; all diagonal numbers with three or more colours; all off-diagonal numbers.
events.directly_checkable: The construction is explicit given the primes (the paper's Lemma 4 combines colourings c_p, with s and Q as above); a reader could check the colourings for small k by computer. Not checked by me.
events.direction: Cuts toward growth of the two-colour diagonal numbers, asymptotically (lower bound). It is stated as verifying Erdos's conjecture that W(k)/2^k tends to infinity. It does not determine any value.
events.object: An explicit family of 2-colourings, one per k, of an interval of length about k·2^(k-1) with no monochromatic k-term progression. Built as a product of Berlekamp-type colourings for a set of primes p (Lemma 4), so the construction is explicit rather than non-constructive. The paper says the coloring was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro.

systems.name: ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: the coloring used to prove Theorem 1, and a proof of Theorem 1, were generated by a query to the model; the abstract says the coloring 'was found by' the model. The authors say the written proof, 'while drawing somewhat on the proof given by ChatGPT', was produced by the authors. The model's proof is therefore part of the argument's provenance, and the paper credits it with the construction the result rests on.
systems.basis_quote: The coloring used to prove Theorem 1, as well as a proof of Theorem 1, were generated by a query to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro.

events.what_happened: H. Cao, 'An improved lower bound for the van der Waerden number w(3,k)', arXiv:2609.31798 (submitted 25 Sep 2026, v1, 13 KB). For k >= 3, w(3,k) is the least n such that every red-blue colouring of [n] has a blue nontrivial 3-term progression or a red nontrivial k-term progression. Result: w(3,k) >= k^(Omega(log k)), improving Hunter's k^(Omega(log k / log log k)) and Green's bound. Abstract page opened; the PDF body not read.
events.delivers: Lower bound for the two-colour mixed number w(3,k), an off-diagonal family; not a diagonal W(r,k). Growth lower bound only; no exact value.
events.remains: All exact values; the diagonal numbers; the upper bound.
events.direction: Off-diagonal lower bound; cuts toward superpolynomial growth; no value; no conflict.

disputes.summary: Erdos Problem 190 (H(k), monochromatic or rainbow progressions): Bae (arXiv 2604.20588, 22 Apr 2026) claims the resolution; the Stanford listing (17 Dec 2025) says Hunter's work gives a quick resolution of problem 190; Fox and Hunter (arXiv 2606.02541, 1 Jun 2026) say they resolve the Erdos-Graham H(k) problem; a search summary of the forum thread for 190 credits Fox and Hunter with a Zenodo proof. The sources conflict on who resolved it first and on which result. This concerns H(k), not the van der Waerden values.

Campos-Fox-Schildkraut: the authors say the coloring and a proof were generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, and that the written proof was produced by the authors, drawing somewhat on the model's proof. A forum post (Xiao Hu, 24 Aug 2026) describes the same bound as 'A new general lower bound by GPT'. The sources differ on how much of the argument the model supplied; the paper's own sentence is the authoritative account.

summary: The Wikipedia article's table of exact values is unchanged in the form I read (fetched page last edited 14 July 2026): seven nontrivial exact values, W(2,3)=9, W(2,4)=35, W(2,5)=178, W(2,6)=1132, W(3,3)=27, W(3,4)=293, W(4,3)=76, with the rest of the table given as lower bounds. Nothing I found since 26 January 2024 determines a new exact value of any W(r,k) or off-diagonal w(r; k_1,...,k_r). The exact values in the table predate 2024 (1978, 2007/2008, 2012), and the one 2026 item that restates an exact value (W(2,5)=178 in Lean, July 2026) re-verifies a 1978 result. The movement is in bounds and in gap results. The strongest bound is Campos, Fox and Schildkraut (arXiv 2608.20824, 21 Aug 2026): w(k) >= (1-o(1))k·2^(k-1) for all k, verifying Erdos's conjecture that W(k)/2^k tends to infinity; the authors say the coloring and a proof were generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, and that the written proof is theirs, drawing somewhat on the model's proof. Fox and Hunter (arXiv 2606.02541, 1 Jun 2026) prove that three-colour numbers grow faster than any exponential in k (w(k;3) > 2^(k log*k/4)); their paper says all mathematical arguments are human-deduced and credits ChatGPT Pro 5.5 only with copyediting. For the difference of consecutive values, DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus has a Lean proof that W(k+1)-W(k) tends to infinity, posted 10 Apr 2026 and reported in arXiv 2605.22763 (21 May 2026, Table 1, asterisked variant of problem 138); two same-day forum comments refine or generalise the gap bound, one crediting GPT-5.4 Thinking. Off-diagonal and multicolour work also moved: Cao (arXiv 2609.31798, 25 Sep 2026) gives w(3,k) >= k^(Omega(log k)); Hunter's 2023 and 2021 papers and Green's 2021 paper sit before the window. Two July 2026 repository claims by Claude (Fable 5) with Abigail Haddad, not reviewed by a mathematician by their own account, give new lower bounds for W(3,19) to W(3,25) and a Lean certificate for W(2,5)=178. Hunter's Stanford talk (17 Dec 2025) described an (r!-o(1))^k lower bound for multicolour diagonal numbers, but no write-up was found. Dates: each event is dated to its first public written argument where I could find it; several pre-2024 dates are years only, and the 2025-12 talk is dated to the talk because no write-up was found. The searches returned no news or expert commentary on the Campos et al. paper, and the Erdos 138 page (last edited 2 June 2026 in the copy I read) does not yet list it. Close calls: (a) whether the 2026 Campos bound moves 'the quantity the problem asks for' (it moves a bound on the diagonal W(2,k), not a value; the two-colour bound is asymptotic and displays no table change); (b) whether the DeepMind difference result touches the problem at all (it concerns the gaps W(k+1)-W(k) of the same sequence, not a value); (c) whether the July 2026 Lean W(2,5)=178 is an event for this problem (it verifies a known value, so it is recorded but changes no entry). I did not find any event that determines a value of W(r,k) newly after 26 January 2024.
competing_reading: For the Campos et al. bound: the problem asks for values, and a bound moves no value, so the result should count as 'nothing new' for the values; the rival reading is that the problem is about the table of W(2,k), and a bound that moves the diagonal two-colour lower bound for every k is a movement of the quantity itself. For the AI provenance of Campos et al.: the authors' sentence that the coloring and 'a proof' were generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro makes the model load-bearing on its face, while their sentence that the written proof was produced by the authors and draws only 'somewhat' on the model's argument supports reading the model as supplying the construction and the authors as supplying the write-up. For the DeepMind difference result: it proves the gaps grow, which some readers would count as progress on the sequence, and others as a result on a different quantity from the values; the paper's own table calls it a variant. For the W(2,5)=178 Lean claim: a reader could count a formal certificate for a known value as a new kind of resolution, but no value changed. For the three-colour Fox–Hunter result: it is a bound on w(k;3), so it may be read as moving the family of diagonal numbers, though the problem as stated asks for two-colour and all-colour values alike and its abstract does not address two colours.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Expert reading of the Campos–Fox–Schildkraut Lemma 4 construction and the full text (PDF body), and a published version or v2 that states whether the model's proof is reproduced or only drawn on. (2) The AlphaProof Nexus Science paper text (8 Oct 2026, reported by secondary sources only) to confirm the 138 variant's statement and the sorry-free status of its helper W_diff_tendsto in the formal-conjectures file. (3) The Sothanaphan notes (Google Drive, sign-in required) and the full forum thread 138. (4) A written argument for Hunter's (r!-o(1))^k claim, or the companion 'via short exact sequences' manuscript. (5) Expert checks of the vdw-records seven lower bounds and of the Lean statement vdw_5_2 : vdwNumber2 5 178. (6) The Mathazine 2024 article for Karki's w(21;2,...,2,3,3)=52, to confirm the value and its date relative to 26 January 2024. (7) The erdosproblems forum thread 190 and the Bae preprint's full text, to settle priority on H(k), if the problem's record is to carry that adjacent claim. (8) Journal publication, or a dated reply from the Wikipedia article's editors, for the Campos paper, which the article table did not yet reflect in the copy I fetched.

event.what_happened: J. Fox and Z. Hunter, 'Three-color van der Waerden numbers grow super-exponentially', arXiv:2606.02541 (submitted 1 Jun 2026, single version, 19 pages). Abstract: for k sufficiently large there is a 3-colouring of about the first 2^(k log*k /4) integers with no monochromatic k-term progression, so w(k;3) > 2^(k log* k /4) (Theorem 1), and a new lower bound on multicolour van der Waerden numbers resolving an Erdos-Graham problem on canonical van der Waerden numbers. The erdosproblems.com entry for 138 cites it as FoHu26. Abstract and HTML read; the PDF body was unreadable through the fetch tool.
event.delivers: Three colours, large k: W(k,3) grows faster than any exponential in k (for the three-colour numbers only). The multicolour canonical result is stated in the abstract as resolving the Erdos-Graham question; its scope beyond the abstract was not read. The two-colour growth question of Erdos (the 500-dollar prize) is not addressed by this paper; the abstract does not mention two colours.
event.remains: Everything in problem_asks except the lower-bound growth for three colours: no exact value; two-colour growth; the rest of the diagonal table; off-diagonal.
event.directly_checkable: The colouring is said to be explicit in the abstract's wording 'we show that there is a three-coloring' (existence). Whether the construction is explicit was not established by me.
event.direction: Lower bound cuts toward growth of three-colour numbers; no value; no conflict with the problem's assertion.
event.object: Three-colouring of an initial segment of length about 2^(k log* k / 4) with no monochromatic k-term progression, for k sufficiently large. Stated as an existence result in the abstract; explicitness not established.

judgement.why: The statement asks for the values of the van der Waerden numbers, a table quantified over all r and k (and, on the article's scope, off-diagonal entries). Each exact value determined is therefore a case, and every growth estimate is a bound. All exact values (W(3,3), W(2,5), W(2,6), W(3,4), Ahmed's off-diagonal values) predate the snapshot. W(4,3) is undated and Karki's 2024 value cannot be placed relative to 26 January, so both get null. After the snapshot nothing determines a value. Campos-Fox-Schildkraut, Fox-Hunter, Cao (w(3,k) is an off-diagonal entry the article tabulates) and the vdw-records W(3,19..25) lower bounds all move bounds on table quantities. The gap results on W(k+1)-W(k) (AlphaProof Nexus, Sothanaphan) answer a different question about differences and are variants; the paper's own table calls 138 a variant. The Lean re-verification of the 1978 W(2,5)=178 is a formalisation of a known result, so it scores none. The Hunter talk has no written argument and also scores none. For AI roles: Campos et al. say the model generated the colouring and a proof, and the authors rewrote the proof drawing on it. Since the construction that the result rests on is the model's, that is generated rather than assisted. vdw-records says everything was produced by Claude, so it is generated. On the variant rows, the forum co-credit to GPT-5.4 is thin but names the model as co-producer of the refinement, so it is assisted.
judgement.doubts: The Campos et al. AI sentences come from a summarising fetch; the generated-versus-assisted call rests on the authors' 'drawing somewhat' phrasing. Treating the difference result as a variant rather than a bound is a judgement call; it would not change the top tier, since other post-snapshot bounds exist. Karki's off-diagonal value, if it is after 26 January 2024 and real, would be a post-snapshot case; it is unverified and undated.
